claims.quote: This document sets forth these final rules related to certain provisions of the No Surprises Act regarding the Federal independent dispute resolution (IDR) process, which was established as part of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 (CAA). These rules finalize new requirements relating to the disclosure of information that group health plans and health insurance issuers offering group or individual health insurance coverage must include along with the initial payment or notice of denial of payment for certain items and services subject to the surprise billing protections in the No Surprises Act.
claims.affected_party: group health plans and health insurance issuers offering group or individual health insurance coverage
claims.summary: Final rules finalize new requirements for disclosure of information with initial payment or notice of denial of payment for certain items and services subject to the surprise billing protections in the No Surprises Act.

claims.quote: These final rules also require plans and issuers to communicate information by using claim adjustment reason codes (CARCs) and remittance advice remark codes (RARCs), as specified in guidance, when providing any paper or electronic remittance advice (ERA) to an entity that does not have a contractual relationship with the plan or issuer.
claims.summary: Final rules require plans and issu,ers to communicate information using CARCs and RARCs when providing remittance advice to entities without a contractual relationship.

claims.quote: This document also finalizes amendments to certain requirements related to the open negotiation period preceding the Federal IDR process, the initiation of the Federal IDR process, the Federal IDR dispute eligibility review process, and the payment and collection of administrative fees and certified IDR entity fees.
claims.summary: Final rules amend requirements related to the open negotiation period, initiation of the Federal IDR process, dispute eligibility review process, and payment and collection of fees.

claims.quote: This document also finalizes the definition of bundled payment arrangements, amends requirements related to batched items and services and amends the rules for extensions of timeframes due to extenuating circumstances.
claims.summary: Final rules finalize the definition of bundled payment arrangements, amend requirements related to batched items and services, and amend rules for extensions of timeframes due to extenuating circumstances.

claims.quote: Additionally, this document finalizes provisions that require plans and issuers to register in the Federal IDR portal.
claims.summary: Final rules require plans and issuers to register in the Federal IDR portal.

claims.quote: each FEHB Program contract must require a carrier to comply with requirements described in sections 9816 and 9817 of the Code, sections 716 and 717 of ERISA, and sections 2799A-1 and 2799A-2 of the PHS Act (as applicable) in the same manner as these provisions apply for a group health plan or health insurance issuer offering group or individual health insurance coverage.
claims.summary: Carriers must comply with specific requirements from sections 9816, 9817, 716, 717, 2799A-1, and 2799A-2 of the Code, ERISA, and PHS Act in the same manner as they apply to group health plans or health insurance issuers.

claims.quote: plans and issuers and nonparticipating providers and facilities may utilize to resolve certain disputes regarding out-of-network rates under section 9816 of the Code, section 716 of ERISA, and section 2799A-1 of the PHS Act.
claims.affected_party: plans and issuers, nonparticipating providers and facilities
claims.summary: Plans and issuers, along with nonparticipating providers and facilities, may utilize the Federal IDR process to resolve disputes regarding out-of-network rates under specified sections.

claims.quote: plans and issuers and nonparticipating providers of air ambulance services to utilize the Federal IDR process.
claims.affected_party: plans and issuers, nonparticipating providers of air ambulance services
claims.summary: Plans and issuers, along with nonparticipating providers of air ambulance services, may utilize the Federal IDR process.

claims.quote: prohibitions on balance billing for certain items and services and requirements related to disclosures about balance billing protections.
claims.affected_party: health care providers, facilities, providers of air ambulance services
claims.summary: Health care providers, facilities, and providers of air ambulance services must comply with prohibitions on balance billing for certain items and services and requirements related to disclosures about balance billing protections.

claims.quote: These rules implement provisions to protect consumers from surprise medical bills for emergency services, non-emergency services furnished by nonparticipating providers for patient visits to participating facilities in certain circumstances, and air ambulance services furnished by nonparticipating providers of air ambulance services.
claims.affected_party: plans and issuers, providers, facilities, providers of air ambulance services
claims.summary: Rules are implemented to protect consumers from surprise medical bills for emergency services, non-emergency services furnished by nonparticipating providers for patient visits to participating facilities in certain circumstances, and air ambulance services furnished by nonparticipating providers of air ambulance services.

claims.quote: These rules also implement provisions to establish a Federal IDR process to determine payment amounts when there is a dispute between plans or issuers and providers, facilities, or providers of air ambulance services about the out-of-network rate for these services in cases where a specified State law or an applicable All-Payer Model Agreement does not provide a method for determining the total amount payable.
claims.affected_party: plans or issuers, providers, facilities, providers of air ambulance services
claims.summary: Rules establish a Federal IDR process to determine payment amounts when there is a dispute between plans or issuers and providers, facilities, or providers of air ambulance services about the out-of-network rate for these services in cases where a specified State law or an applicable All-Payer Model Agreement does not provide a method for determining the total amount payable.

claims.quote: The disclosure requirements at 45 CFR 149.430 regarding patient protections against balance billing are applicable as of January 1, 2022.
claims.summary: The disclosure requirements at 45 CFR 149.430 regarding patient protections against balance billing are applicable as of January 1, 2022.

claims.quote: A dispute is not eligible for the Federal IDR process unless it concerns an item or service that meets the definition of a qualified IDR item or service. 29 CFR 2590.716-8(a)(2)(xi) and 45 CFR 149.510 (a)(2)(xi).
claims.summary: A dispute is not eligible for the Federal IDR process unless it concerns an item or service that meets the definition of a qualified IDR item or service.

claims.quote: Disputes are also ineligible when the disputing parties initiate the Federal IDR process after failing to satisfy the 30-business-day open negotiation period requirements specified under 29 CFR 2590.716-8(b)(1) and 45 CFR 149.510(b)(1) or after 4 business days after the end of the 30-business-day open negotiation period as specified under 29 CFR 2590.716-8(b)(2)(i) and 45 CFR 149.510(b)(2)(i).
claims.summary: Disputes are ineligible if the disputing parties initiate the Federal IDR process after failing to satisfy the 30-business-day open negotiation period requirements or after 4 business days after the end of the 30-business-day open negotiation period.

claims.quote: 29 CFR 2590.716-8(c)(3)(i)(B) and 45 CFR 149.510(c)(3)(i)(B). The District Court vacated the batching provisions of 45 CFR 149.510(c)(3)(i)(C), 26 CFR 54.9816-8T(c)(3)(i)(C), and 29 CFR 2590.716-8(c)(3)(i)(C) in Tex. Med. Ass'n v. U.S. Dep't of Health & Hum. Servs., Case No. 6:23-cv-59-JDK (E.D. Tex. Aug. 3, 2023) (TMA IV).
claims.summary: The batching provisions of 45 CFR 149.510(c)(3)(i)(C), 26 CFR 54.9816-8T(c)(3)(i)(C), and 29 CFR 2590.716-8(c)(3)(i)(C) were vacated by the District Court.

The Departments have implemented Federal IDR portal system enhancements, such as enabling non-initiating parties to submit supporting documentation to contest dispute eligibility within their response to the notice of IDR initiation and requiring non-initiating parties to attest to the health plan type.

claims.quote: requiring that these parties share specific information before initiating the Federal IDR process, including by providing No Surprises Act-specific claim adjustment reason codes (CARCs) and remittance advice remark codes (RARCs) with a remittance advice.
claims.summary: Plans, issuers, and providers must share specific information before initiating the Federal IDR process, including providing No Surprises Act-specific claim adjustment reason codes (CARCs) and remittance advice remark codes (RARCs) with a remittance advice.

claims.quote: amend the information that must be disclosed about the QPA.
claims.summary: The information that must be disclosed about the QPA must be amended.

claims.quote: require plans and issuers to register with the Federal IDR portal to facilitate identification of the parties to a dispute and determine whether coverage of an item or service that is the subject of the dispute is subject to a specified State law, an All-Payer Model Agreement, or the Federal IDR process for determining the out-of-network rate.
claims.summary: Plans and issu,ers must register with the Federal IDR portal to facilitate identification of the parties to a dispute and determine whether coverage of an item or service that is the subject of the dispute is subject to a specified State law, an All-Payer Model Agreement, or the Federal IDR process for determining the out-of-network rate.

claims.quote: amend to the content requirements of the standard open negotiation notice, establish requirements related to an open negotiation response notice, and clarify the timing for when the open negotiation period begins.
claims.summary: The content requirements of the standard open negotiation notice must be amended, requirements related to an open negotiation response notice must be established, and the timing for when the open negotiation period begins must be clarified.

claims.quote: include amendments to the notice of IDR initiation and new requirements for the initiation response from the non-initiating party.
claims.summary: Amendments to the notice of IDR initiation and new requirements for the initiation response from the non-initiating party must be included.

claims.quote: The 2023 proposed rules also proposed to establish a standard process for disputes to be withdrawn from the Federal IDR process.
claims.summary: Establish a standard process for disputes to be withdrawn from the Federal IDR process.

claims.quote: The Departments also proposed reduced administrative fee amounts for non-initiating parties in cases of ineligible disputes as well as pursuing Federal debt collection of the administrative fee from parties that do not pay as required.
claims.summary: Pursue Federal debt collection of the administrative fee from parties that do not pay as required.

claims.quote: The Departments proposed to amend requirements related to batched items and services and bundled payment arrangements. These amendments sought to provide clarity in how parties can submit multiple items and services as either batched items and services or bundled payment arrangements in a single dispute and to provide additional flexibility in submitting multiple items and services.
claims.summary: Amend requirements related to batched items and services and bundled payment arrangements to provide clarity and flexibility in submitting multiple items and services.

claims.quote: The proposed rules also proposed to expand upon situations in which timeframes may be waived due to extenuating circumstances.
claims.summary: Expand upon situations in which timeframes may be waived due to extenuating circumstances.

claims.quote: The Departments received 124 timely comments during both comment periods ⌒ in response to the proposed rules from a wide variety of interested parties...
claims.summary: Provide detailed feedback on multiple aspects of the proposed rules and in response to various specific comment solicitations.

claims.quote: The Departments are finalizing the 2023 proposed rules, with some changes in response to comments as described in more detail later in this preamble, to improve the overall functioning of the Federal IDR process.
claims.summary: Finalize the 2023 proposed rules with changes in response to comments to improve the overall functioning of the Federal IDR process.

claims.quote: The Departments shall provide that, in the case of items and services which are included by a provider or facility as part of a bundled payment, such items and services may be part of a single determination.
claims.summary: The Departments must provide that items and services included in a bundled payment may be part of a single determination.

claims.quote: The October 2021 interim final rules specify that in the case of qualified IDR items and services billed by a provider, facility, or provider of air ambulance services as part of a bundled payment arrangement, or if a plan or issuer makes or denies an initial payment as a bundled payment, the qualified IDR items and services may be submitted as part of one dispute and are subject to the rules for batched disputes and the certified IDR entity fee for single disputes.
claims.affected_party: provider, facility, provider of air ambulance services, plan or issuer
claims.summary: Qualified IDR items and services billed as part of a bundled payment arrangement may be submitted as part of one dispute and are subject to the rules for batched disputes and the certified IDR entity fee for single disputes.

claims.quote: The Departments provided a definition for a bundled arrangement in the August 2022 Technical Assistance for Certified IDR Entities.
claims.summary: The Departments must provide a definition for a bundled arrangement in the August 2022 Technical Assistance for Certified IDR Entities.

claims.quote: The 2023 proposed rules proposed to codify the definition set forth in the August 2022 Technical Assistance for Certified IDR Entities.
claims.summary: The 2023 proposed rules proposed to codify the definition set forth in the August 2022 Technical Assistance for Certified IDR Entities.

claims.quote: a provider, facility, or provider of air ambulance services bills for multiple items or services furnished to a single patient under a single service code that represents multiple items or services (for example, a diagnostic related group (DRG) code); or (2) a plan or issuer makes an initial payment or notice of denial of payment to a provider, facility, or provider of air ambulance services under a single service code that represents multiple items or services furnished to a single patient (for example, a DRG code).
claims.affected_party: provider, facility, provider of air ambulance services, plan or issuer
claims.summary: A provider, facility, or provider of air ambulance services must bill for multiple items or services under a single service code, or a plan or issuer must make an initial payment or notice of denial under a single service code representing multiple items or services.

claims.quote: the Departments proposed to remove the language under 26 CFR 54.9816-8T(c)(3)(ii), 29 CFR 2590.716-8(c)(3)(ii), and 45 CFR 149.510(c)(3)(ii) stating that a bundled payment arrangement is subject to the rules for batched disputes.
claims.summary: The Departments proposed to remove the language stating that a bundled payment arrangement is subject to the rules for batched disputes.

claims.quote: the Departments are finalizing the definition of the term ``bundled payment arrangement'' at 26 CFR 54.9816-3, 29 CFR 2590.716-3, and 45 CFR 149.30 as proposed.
claims.summary: The Departments are finalizing the definition of the term ``bundled payment arrangement'' as proposed.

claims.quote: the Departments did not receive any comments on the proposed amendment to remove the language under 26 CFR 54.9816-8T(c)(3)(ii), 29 CFR 2590.716-8(c)(3)(ii), and 45 CFR 149.510(c)(3)(ii) stating that a bundled payment arrangement is subject to the rules for batched disputes, and are finalizing this amendment as proposed.
claims.summary: The Departments are finalizing the amendment to remove the language stating that a bundled payment arrangement is subject to the rules for batched disputes.

claims.quote: creates an administrative barrier to submitting a bundled dispute and could disincentivize parties from using or relying on bundled payment arrangements, which could decrease the accessibility of the Federal IDR process for bundled payment arrangements.
claims.summary: Parties must not create administrative barriers to submitting bundled disputes, as this could disincentivize the use of bundled payment arrangements and decrease accessibility to the Federal IDR process.

claims.quote: All ERAs must comply with the Accredited Standards Committee (ASC) X12 835 transaction standard adopted by HHS under 45 CFR 162.1602.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must comply with the ASC X12 835 transaction standard adopted by HHS under 45 CFR 162.1602 when transmitting explanations of benefits (EOBs) or remittance advice information.

claims.quote: The ASC X12 835 implementation guide mandates the use of CARCs and RARCs to communicate remittance information (as opposed to any other code systems, such as proprietary codes developed by specific plans and
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must use CARCs and RARCs to communicate remittance information, as opposed to any other code systems, such as proprietary codes developed by specific plans and.

claims.quote: The HIPAA operating rule adopted at 45 CFR 162.1603(a)(4) requires plans and issuers to use a uniform set of CARCs and RARCs for defined business scenarios.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must use a uniform set of CARCs and RARCs for defined business scenarios.

claims.quote: Any interested party can use publicly available forms to submit requests for new or modified CARCs and RARCs and accompanying explanations to the respective committees on a rolling basis.
claims.summary: Interested parties must use publicly available forms to submit requests for new or modified CARCs and RARCs and accompanying explanations to the respective committees on a rolling basis.

claims.quote: Updated lists of approved CARCs and RARCs, along with an updated list of approved CARC and RARC combinations and business scenarios, are published three times each year.
claims.summary: Updated lists of approved CARCs and RARCs, along with an updated list of approved CARC and RARC combinations and business scenarios, must be published three times each year.

claims.quote: the July 2021 interim final rules also applied the requirement to make disclosures regarding the QPA for providers of air ambulance services.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must make disclosures regarding the QPA for providers of air ambulance services.

claims.quote: These proposals would require plans and issuers to use CARCs and RARCs, as specified in guidance issued by the Departments, or as required under any applicable adopted standards and operating rules under 45 CFR part 162, to communicate information related to whether a claim for an item or service furnished by an entity that does not have a direct or indirect contractual relationship with the plan or issuer for the furnishing of such item or service under the plan or coverage is subject to the provisions of 26 CFR 54.9816 and 54.9817; 2, 2590.716 and 2590.717; or 45 CFR part 149, subpart B, E, or F.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must use CARCs and RARCs to communicate information related to whether a claim for an item or service is subject to specific provisions.

claims.quote: the Departments are finalizing the CARC and RARC proposal with minor modifications.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must finalize the CARC and RARC proposal with minor modifications.

claims.quote: the requirement to use specified CARCs and RARCs under these final rules will be in addition to the disclosure requirements at 26 CFR 54.9816-6(d), 29 CFR 2590.716-6(d), and 45 CFR 149.140(d) and Federal IDR registry requirements at 26 CFR 54.9816-9, 29 CFR 2590.716-9, and 45 CFR 149.530.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must use specified CARCs and RARCs in addition to existing disclosure and Federal IDR registry requirements.

claims.quote: The Departments proposed in the 2023 proposed rules that the requirements under 26 CFR 54.9816-6A, 29 CFR 2590.716-6A, and 45 CFR 149.100 relating to CARCs and RARCs would apply to plans and issuers when sending any paper or electronic remittance advice to entities with which they do not have a direct or indirect contractual relationship, including for items and services to which the No Surprises Act surprise billing requirements do not apply.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must apply CARC and RARC requirements when sending remittance advice to entities without a direct or indirect contractual relationship, including for items and services not subject to the No Surprises Act.

claims.quote: The Departments acknowledge these final rules may require some plans and issuers to implement new processes to include CARCs and RARCs related to the No Surprises Act on remittance advice but have determined that there is a critical need to provide this information to improve the functioning of the Federal IDR process.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must implement new processes to include CARCs and RARCs related to the No Surprises Act on remittance advice.

claims.quote: it is equally important to understand when an item or service is not subject to these protections, so that parties can take appropriate steps to resolve payment issues and avoid submission of ineligible disputes to the Federal IDR process.
claims.summary: Parties must understand when an item or service is not subject to the protections to resolve payment issues and avoid submitting ineligible disputes to the Federal IDR process.

claims.quote: the Departments are finalizing this aspect of the proposed requirements as proposed.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must finalize the aspect of the proposed requirements related to CARCs and RARCs on remittance advice.

claims.quote: the Departments sought comment on whether a plan or issuer should generate a remittance advice that can be obtained upon request by the provider when the plan or issuer makes a payment directly to a participant, beneficiary, or enrollee, and whether the proposed requirement to use CARCs and RARCs to convey No Surprises Act-specific information should apply in these circumstances.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must consider whether to generate a remittance advice upon request by the provider and whether the requirement to use CARCs and RARCs applies in these circumstances.

claims.quote: In these cases, the plan or issuer would be required to provide an updated remittance advice to the provider that includes any relevant required CARCs or RARCs.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must provide an updated remittance advice to the provider that includes any relevant required CARCs or RARCs when there is a revision in the assessment of an item or service.

claims.quote: These final rules do not require plans and issuers to use CARCs and RARCs on remittance advice for payments made directly to participants, beneficiaries, or enrollees--including if the remittance advice is requested by the provider that furnished the item or service for which payment is made.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers are prohibited from using CARCs and RARCs on remittance advice for payments made directly to participants, beneficiaries, or enrollees.

claims.quote: These final rules establish the general requirement that plans and issuers use CARCs and RARCs, in the manner and timeframe specified in guidance, to communicate information about whether an item or service identified on a claim is or is not subject to the surprise billing requirements under the No Surprises Act.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must use CARCs and RARCs, in the manner and timeframe specified in guidance, to communicate information about whether an item or service is subject to the surprise billing requirements under the No Surprises Act.

claims.quote: Future guidance will identify the specific CARCs and RARCs to be used in particular circumstances, which, as discussed below in section II.B.2.e of this preamble, when surprise billing protections do apply, may include use of CARCs and RARCs to communicate relevant procedural or administrative information related to application of the surprise billing protections to the items or services at issue.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must use CARCs and RARCs to communicate relevant procedural or administrative information related to the application of surprise billing protections to items or services when such protections apply.

claims.quote: Future guidance will also provide any administrative and technical instructions necessary to facilitate the use of mandated CARCs and RARCs in all paper or electronic remittance advice transactions to providers that do not have a contractual relationship with the plan or issuer.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must use mandated CARCs and RARCs in all paper or electronic remittance advice transactions to providers that do not have a contractual relationship with the plan or issuer.

claims.quote: Commenters recommended that any guidance should include explicit timelines for compliance and provide clear direction for how specified CARCs and RARCs must be used.
claims.summary: The Departments must include explicit timelines for compliance and provide clear direction for how specified CARCs and RARCs must be used.

claims.quote: Commenters requested that guidance address potential non-compliance, including describing oversight mechanisms and penalties and providing contact information for filing complaints against parties that are non-compliant with the CARC and RARC requirement.
claims.summary: The Departments must address potential non-compliance by describing oversight mechanisms and penalties and providing contact information for filing complaints against non-compliant parties.

claims.quote: The Departments have determined that guidance, rather than notice-and-comment rulemaking, is appropriate for providing the technical and operational instruction needed to implement this provision.
claims.summary: The Departments must use guidance rather than notice-and-comment rulemaking to provide technical and operational instruction for implementing the provision.

claims.quote: This approach will provide necessary flexibility, enabling the Departments to better respond to evolving needs and circumstances, including the flexibility to discontinue specification of certain CARCs and RARCs should the information they communicate become readily available to providers through a different mechanism or otherwise become unnecessary.
claims.summary: The Departments must maintain flexibility to discontinue specification of certain CARCs and RARCs if the information they communicate becomes readily available through a different mechanism or becomes unnecessary.

claims.quote: The Departments have determined that because all plans and issuers that provide ERA transactions that are subject to the HIPAA Administrative Simplification requirements are required to use CARCs and RARCs, most plans and issuers already have the capacity to implement the CARC and RARC requirement.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers that provide ERA transactions subject to HIPAA Administrative Simplification requirements are required to use CARCs and RARCs.

claims.quote: Plans and issuers will not be required to use CARCs and RARCs under these final rules until such date as provided for in future guidance.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers are not required to use CARCs and RARCs until a future date specified in guidance.

claims.quote: the Departments will consider providing technical direction in future guidance to facilitate implementation of the CARC and RARC requirements on ERA with limited space available for data elements.
claims.summary: The Departments will consider providing technical direction in future guidance to facilitate implementation of the CARC and RARC requirements on ERA with limited space available for data elements.

claims.quote: the Departments are aware that after guidance is issued identifying the specific CARCs and RARCs required to be used, plans and issuers will need additional time to implement the CARC and RARC requirement.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers will need additional time to implement the CARC and RARC requirement after guidance is issued identifying the specific CARCs and RARCs required to be used.
